messages:
sanya: Heads-up — after last night's mlx5 firmware + OFED 5.9.x rollout in euc1 we're seeing a ~40-50% drop in NCCL AllReduce bandwidth on the p4d pools. Tests show much higher CPU on one side of the net stack. Anyone seen this?

luke: which firmware/driver exactly? kernel version? has this been rolled out to all racks or just a subset?

sanya: rollout tag is fw-mlx5-2026-03-17 + ofed-5.9.1. Kernel 6.1.0-102-generic on these hosts. Canary was 10 nodes, then 120 nodes last night.

maria: saw a small blip in eu-west (smaller fleets) but not as bad as euc1. could be traffic pattern differences.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: fw-mlx5-2026-03-17 applied to rack-euc1-3, rack-euc1-4, rack-euc1-7 at 2026-03-17T23:12:02Z

luke: can you paste a quick nccl-test before/after? and an ethtool -c / -S for the mlx5 interface?

sanya: here's a quick reproducer run on one node (before = baseline from last week):

```
# before (baseline)
AllReduce size 8MB: 7100 MB/s
AllReduce size 64MB: 6900 MB/s

# after firmware
AllReduce size 8MB: 3800 MB/s
AllReduce size 64MB: 3600 MB/s
```

sanya: ethtool -c eth0 output on a bad host:

```
Coalesce parameters for eth0:
rx-usecs: 125
rx-frames: 0
tx-usecs: 0
tx-frames: 0
adaptive-rx: off
adaptive-tx: off
```

luke: rx-usecs 125 is very high. MLX5 firmware/driver sometimes enables interrupt coalescing by default on newer fw. Can you try disabling it (rx-usecs 0) and retest? Also check irqbalance and inflight NAPI settings.

maria: also check mlx5_core interrupts pinned to CPU cores used by NCCL — if interrupts are hot on the same CPU as user-space threads, perf will show high irq/softirq.

sanya: ran quick tweak on one canary node:

```
sudo systemctl stop irqbalance
sudo ethtool -C eth0 rx-usecs 0 rx-frames 1
# re-run nccl-tests
```

sanya: result: AllReduce 8MB: 6300 MB/s, 64MB: 6100 MB/s. Not fully back to baseline but much improved.

ops-oncall: that's promising. What's the rollout impact? How many jobs affected and estimated GPU-hours lost?

sanya: approx 25% of p4d capacity in euc1 saw the drop for ~4 hours before alerts. Estimated ~180 GPU-hours extra due to slower runs and retries :grimacing: 

luke: agree we shouldn't rollback whole region immediately. Plan: 1) change coalescing defaults at kernel/udev for affected NICs for all canary hosts, 2) collect perf traces (perf record, softirq hist) and ethtool -S counters, 3) open ticket with vendor with logs. If coalescing change fully restores perf on canary, schedule phased rollback of firmware.

maria: add checking of mlx5 mmap and flow steering counters too. Also test sustained multi-node NCCL (not just single node nsight) — NCCL is sensitive to tail latency.

sanya: collecting traces now. attaching short dmesg snippet from one host before tweak:

```
[    7.123456] mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: NIC X firmware 23.56.0 loaded
[   12.654321] mlx5_core: IRQ 45 affinity: cpu0
[  210.987654] net_ratelimit: 100 callbacks suppressed
```

infra-bot: perf-bot: started perf collection on node-241 for 30m (job id perf-1825004321-241)

luke: can you also test turning adaptive-rx on? sometimes adaptive-rx works better than hard zero depending on traffic mix. But rx-usecs 125 definitely looks wrong for RL/low-latency RDMA workloads.

sanya: tried adaptive-rx on one host — marginally better than 125, but not as good as rx-usecs=0. Will keep both configs in experiments.

ops-oncall: please prepare rollback runbook if vendor can't provide a fix quickly. Include steps to pin previous firmware and verify PCI IDs. Who owns that?

luke: infra-ml owns the rollback. I'll make a draft runbook on the ticket and tag fw-team and hw-ops. Steps: identify nodes with fw-mlx5-2026-03-17, schedule maintenance window, flash previous fw (fw-mlx5-2026-02-28), reboot, verify ethtool -c and nccl perf on a smoke job.

sanya: creating ticket with perf artifacts and canary numbers and linking this thread. Also pushing udev rule to set rx-usecs=0 on canaries for next boot.

maria: +1. Let's also add a firewall to the rollout: pause any further fw rollouts until vendor triage or we've validated a safe config.

sanya: noted. Pausing euc1 rollout tag in deploy system now. :thumbsup:

luke: thanks — if anyone sees other odd net metrics (packet drops, rx errors), paste ethtool -S and `cat /proc/interrupts`. That helps vendor reproduce.

sanya: will post full artifacts in the ticket when perf job completes. Thanks all.
